newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: ARNOTTS RECALL "BAD DAY FOR AUSTRALIA"
The managing director of Arnotts Biscuits says the recall of the company's products in two states in response to an extortion threat, marks a bad day for the Australian community.
Extortionists have threatened to place poisoned biscuits on supermarket shelves in Queensland and New South Wales from Monday.
That's unless detectives who gave evidence in a Brisbane murder trial take a lie detector test.
The trial in 1993 led to a jail term for Ronald Henry Thomas for the murder of a Gold Coast couple.
Arnotts head Chris Roberts says it's a bad day for Arnotts, the Australian food industry and the Australian community.
Police in New South Wales are searching for John Victor Bobak in connection with the poisoning threats.
Police say at this stage there is no danger to the community from the threats.
Arnotts has set up a customer call centre on 1800 353 255.
NATIONAL AUSTRALIA CUTS INTEREST RATE
The battle for the hearts and minds of home mortgagees has taken another step.
The National Australia Bank has responded to the Commonwealth's move earlier this week, matching its interest rate cut on a standard variable loan.
The rate's been reduced from 8.25 to 7.55 percent, effective from next Monday for new customers, and April the 17th for existing ones.
PASMINCO EXPECTS TO PROCEED WITH CENTURY ZINC DEAL
The Century Zinc mine project in Queensland has been delayed for at least another six months.
The Pasminco company has confirmed its agreement to purchase Century Zinc from the RTZ-CRA group, accomodates native title issues but because agreement can't be reached these will now be arbitrated.
CRA offered a 60-million dollar compensation package but the offer has lapsed and the matter will go before the Native Title Tribunal for arbitration.
BRYANT SNUBBED BY OTHER INMATES
Some inmates of Hobart's Risdon Prison have snubbed mass murderer Martin Bryant, as prison authorities have tried to integrate him into the prison system.
Bryant is being held at the prison hospital after being sentenced to life imprisonment for the Port Arthur shootings last year.
The head of Corrective Services, Denbeigh Richards, says the difficulties assimilating Bryant into the general prison population were not unexpected and the process will take some time.
He has also confirmed that somebody took an unauthorised photograph of Bryant last year but says the film was destroyed before it could be smuggled out of the prison.
NO RESIGNATION FROM GABI HOLLOWS
The Director of the Fred Hollows Foundation, Mike Lynskey, has clarified his position and now says Gabi Hollows has not resigned.
Earlier today, Mr Lynskey said Ms Hollows had decided to leave the Foundation, because of the row over her role on the Civil Aviation Safety Authority Board.
Mr Lynskey says he's since spoken to Ms Hollows who told him she's not leaving the Hollows Foundation.
HINCHINBROOK RESORT CHALLENGE DISMISSED
A Federal Court judge says the Environment Minister did not misinterpret his powers when he approved the Port Hinchinbrook resort development in far north Queensland last year.
Justice Ronald Sackville has dismissed an appeal by the Friends of Hinchinbrook Society against the multi million dollar project which is near a world heritage listed area.
The Society questioned the approval given to the dredging of a marina, and the removal and pruning of mangroves.
Justice Sackville said he concluded that the Minister, Robert Hill, did not take into account irrelevant considerations, and that other challenges to the minister's decisions were not well founded.
In a first for the Federal Court in Australia, the judge allowed his judgement to be recorded by television and radio.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
